description: Welcome to AstroMinds! We are computer science students at Coimbatore building an innovative space tech prototype. We are looking for passionate teammates with coding and AI/ML skills to join us!
summary: ASTROHEALTH is a health monitoring and mission support platform designed to help monitor astronaut well-being during space missions. It brings together simulated astronaut health measurements, digital twin visualization, ECG monitoring, sleep and behavioral health indicators, radiation and space-weather information, and decision-support features in one dashboard. The system is designed to help identify unusual health patterns and present useful information to support mission monitoring. It also explores NASA space-weather and space biology research resources through dedicated data modules. The platform combines an interactive interface, data visualization, and explainable alerts to make complex health information easier to understand. It is a prototype: astronaut biometric readings are simulated and its alerts are not medically validated. ASTROHEALTH aims to support safer, more informed health monitoring during long-duration space missions.
details:
1. Project Overview

ASTROHEALTH is a web-based astronaut health monitoring and mission support system designed for long-duration space missions. It brings important astronaut health indicators and space-related information together in one interactive dashboard.

2. How It Works

The platform provides simulated astronaut profiles and health measurements, including heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), blood oxygen (SpO2), blood pressure, and ECG visualization. A digital twin interface helps users explore astronaut health status.

It also includes modules for sleep and behavioral health, cardiovascular monitoring, cranial health, musculoskeletal health, and radiation-related space-weather information. An anomaly monitoring feature highlights unusual patterns and provides decision-support information for mission monitoring.

NASA data modules are designed to explore space-weather information from NASA DONKI and space biology research resources from NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR).

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTROHEALTH aims to make astronaut health information easier to understand and monitor. It brings multiple types of information into one interface, helps users explore possible health-related patterns, and supports awareness of potential issues during long-duration missions. It may also help students and researchers understand the challenges of astronaut health monitoring.

4. Technology Used

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It uses interactive charts, data visualization, and state management to present information. NASA data services are included for exploring DONKI space-weather events and OSDR research resources.

5. Creativity and Innovation

The main innovation is combining astronaut health visualization, digital twin concepts, space-weather information, research exploration, and explainable monitoring features in a single platform. The design focuses on making complex information accessible through an interactive dashboard.

6. Current Limitations

ASTROHEALTH is a prototype. The astronaut biometric readings are simulated and are not collected from real astronauts or medical devices. Its alerts are experimental decision-support features, not medically validated diagnoses or flight medical advice. NASA space-weather events are not direct measurements of an individual astronaut's radiation dose.
